Thesis_Replication – User Guide

An R folder that reproduces the main results of the empirical chapters of Imperfect Credibility at the Effective Lower Bound

Author

Lloyd Allotey

Published

November 11, 2026

0 Overview

Thesis_Replication is the R folder behind the empirical chapters of the bachelor thesis Imperfect Credibility at the Effective Lower Bound: A Behavioural Macroeconomic Analysis of Eurozone Inflation Expectations (University of St. Gallen, November 2026). Two scripts do the work. build_database.R turns the raw downloads into a DuckDB database once. main.R reads that database, classifies the forecasters of the ECB Survey of Professional Forecasters (SPF), estimates the two behavioural parameters of the expectations block and evaluates both models against the SPF mean.

Research question of the thesis:

To what extent does a time varying perceived inflation anchor improve the ability of the expectations block of a Behavioural New Keynesian model to explain euro area inflation expectations, particularly at the effective lower bound, and does any potential gain stem from the anchor itself or from agents switching between forecasting rules?

Model A is centred on the announced target of 2%. Model B is centred on the perceived anchor built from the 5y5y inflation-linked swap rate. Model S, centred on the mean SPF five-year-ahead forecast, is the robustness check.

With its default parameters main.R reproduces Tables 4.2, 5.3 to 5.7, 6.1 to 6.4 and J.1 and Figures 4.1 to 4.3, 5.1 to 5.4, J.1 and J.2. Not in the package are Table 4.3 and Figure 4.4 (capture ratios), Figures J.3 and J.4 and the dashed Wald curves of Figure 5.2.

1 Getting started

1.1 Requirements

  • R 4.4 or 4.5 and RStudio
  • An internet connection for the first start, when renv installs the packages
  • No build tools. The packages come ready-built for Windows and macOS

1.2 Install

Extract the archive, open Thesis_Replication.Rproj in RStudio and run this once in the console:

renv::restore(prompt = FALSE)

It installs the package versions of renv.lock into a project library and takes about a minute. On a Mac, unzip to Documents rather than Downloads.

1.3 First run

Open main.R and source it (the Source button, or Ctrl+Shift+S). The default run takes about two and a half minutes. Tables appear in the console, figures in the Plots pane. Nothing is written to disk.

1.4 Changing a parameter

Every parameter sits in Part I of main.R with its thesis value in a comment. Change a value and source the script again. Every table and figure follows. At the end the script lists the parameters that differ from the thesis and checks Table 5.6 against the thesis values.

1.5 Rebuild the database (optional)

source("build_database.R")

The database ships ready, so this step is only needed if a raw file is replaced. The script reads the raw files in data/raw/, saves every cleaning step as its own table and prints the checks of the data chapter. It takes under a minute.

2 How the folder is organised

File Purpose
main.R The analysis, one script read top to bottom
build_database.R Builds data/thesis.duckdb from data/raw/
data/raw/ The raw downloads as obtained
data/thesis.duckdb The database, 13 tables (Section 6)
notebooks/user_guide.qmd This guide, rendered to user_guide.html
renv.lock, renv/activate.R, .Rprofile The package versions
README.md How to run it, in short

main.R has ten parts. They are RStudio sections, so the document outline (Ctrl+Shift+O) jumps between them.

Part What it does Main objects
Set up Loads the packages
I Parameters anchor, score, delta, the switches, baseline, this_run
II Input checks
III Loads the data, builds the centres, calibrates the constants panel, rounds, premium, models
IV Model functions the functions of Section 4
V Classification, Table 4.2 classified, shares
VI Estimation, Table 5.3 fit, results
VII Evaluation, Tables 5.4, 5.6 and 5.7
VIII Side analyses, Tables 5.5 and 6.1 to 6.4, and Table J.1 real_time_biases
IX Comparison with the thesis changed, comparison
X Figures 4.1 to 4.3, 5.1 to 5.4, J.1 and J.2

Every table and figure stays in the workspace as an object. Its name starts with the thesis number and ends with a word for its content, for example table_5_6_gain or fig_5_2_profiles.

build_database.R has eleven parts in the same style, one per source and cleaning step.

3 Parameter reference (Part I of main.R)

Data inputs.

Parameter Thesis value Meaning
DB_FILE "data/thesis.duckdb" The database
TABLE_PANEL, TABLE_ROUNDS "estimation_panel", "rounds" The two tables the script reads

Four switches change the specification.

Parameter Thesis value Meaning
anchor "ILS" Centre of the second model. "ILS" gives Model B, "LTSPF" gives Model S
score "saturating" Performance score. "saturating" is Equation 5.2, "msfe" the squared error
bias_statistic "median" Statistic of the biases (Equation 5.5), "median" or "mean"
bias_window "complete" Rounds the biases are calibrated on. "complete" is the whole sample, "pre ELB" the rounds before elb_from

Centres, sample and regimes.

Parameter Thesis value Meaning
target 2 Announced target, in %. It also sets the level of Model B’s centre
first_round, last_round "2004Q3", "2026Q2" Estimation window, 88 rounds
bench_from, bench_to "2004Q3", "2014Q2" Normalisation window of the perceived anchor (Equation 3.2)
elb_from, elb_to "2014Q3", "2022Q2" ELB regime (Table 3.4)
horizon 4 Rounds between a forecast and its evaluation

Calibrated constants. NA takes the value the thesis calibrates from the data. A number overrides that one constant and leaves the others unchanged, so the run shows its effect all else equal.

Parameter Default Meaning
delta NA (0.2824) Half width of the targeter band (Equation 4.3)
E_star NA (3.11) Threshold between ordinary and extreme errors (Equation 5.7)
tau NA (0.399) Scale of the saturating score (Equation 5.6)
w NA (0.101) Weight of the squared error (Equation 5.6)
bias_up, bias_down NA per model Hawk and dove bias. NA calibrates it (Equation 5.5), a number fixes it
U_0 0 Performance of every heuristic before the first evaluation

Optimiser and side analyses.

Parameter Thesis value Meaning
quick_mode FALSE FALSE uses 300 starting values, TRUE 30. The package ships with TRUE, which gives the same estimates
gamma_start_range, rho_start_range c(0.01, 100), c(0, 0.98) Ranges of the starting values
run_feasibility TRUE Table 5.5
run_anchors TRUE Table 6.1
run_delta TRUE Table 6.2
run_score TRUE Table 6.3
run_biases TRUE Table 6.4, the real-time rows of Table J.1 and Figures J.1 and J.2

4 Function reference (Part IV of main.R)

Three arguments recur. model is a model letter, "A", "B" or "S". data is the list returned by prepare(). score_set holds the settings of the score, made by score_settings(). Examples follow in Section 5.

4.1 Classification and data of a model

[1] classify(forecast, centre, delta)

  • Assign each forecast to a type around its centre (Equation 4.1).

Arguments

  • forecast, centre : numeric vectors of the same length.
  • delta : numeric, half width of the targeter band.

Returns

  • A character vector with "hawk", "targeter" or "dove".

[2] classify_panel(model, delta)

  • Classify the whole panel around the centre of one model. The only place where forecasts are classified.

Returns

  • The panel with the columns model, regime, centre and type.

[3] prepare(model, delta, b_up, b_down, statistic, window, same_rounds)

  • Classify the forecasts around a centre, calibrate the two biases (Equation 5.5, done by calibrate_biases()) and collect the data of the scored rounds.

Arguments

  • model, delta as above.
  • b_up, b_down : numeric or NA, default the biases of Part I. NA calibrates the bias.
  • statistic, window : character, default the two bias switches of Part I. window = "real time" gives real-time biases (Table 6.4).
  • same_rounds : logical. TRUE scores constant biases on the rounds that real-time biases can use.

Returns

  • A list with the counts per round, the centres, realised inflation, the SPF mean and the two biases.

[4] score_settings(tau, w, msfe = FALSE)

  • Bundle the settings of the performance score.

Returns

  • list(tau, w, msfe). With msfe = TRUE the score is the squared error.

4.2 The expectations block

[5] probabilities(gamma, rho, data, score_set)

  • The shares of the hawk, targeter and dove heuristic in every scored round (Equations 5.1 to 5.4).

The errors \(e\) of the three heuristics against realised inflation are scored by

\[ \psi(e) = \frac{e^2}{e^2 + \tau^2} + w\,e^2, \]

accumulated into the performance \(U_t = \rho\,U_{t-1} - (1 - \rho)\,\psi(e_t)\) and turned into shares by the multinomial logit.

Arguments

  • gamma, rho : numeric, intensity of choice and memory.

Returns

  • A matrix, one row per scored round, three columns that sum to one.

[6] minus_loglik(par, data, score_set)

  • Minus the multinomial log-likelihood (Equation 5.8), the objective of the optimiser.

Arguments

  • par : numeric(2), c(gamma, rho).

Returns

  • One number, 1e12 outside \(\gamma\) in [0, 1000] and \(\rho\) in [0, 0.999).

4.3 Estimation

[7] starting_values(n_gamma, n_rho)

  • The starting grid, log-spaced \(\gamma\) times evenly spaced \(\rho\).

Returns

  • A data frame with the columns gamma and rho.

[8] estimate(data, score_set, starts)

  • Nelder-Mead from every starting value, each search restarted once.

Returns

  • A list with gamma, rho, loglik and searches, the end point of every search.

[9] dispersion(data, prob)

  • The dispersion factor \(\hat\varphi\) (Equation 5.10).

Returns

  • One number, 15.35 for Model A and 15.36 for Model B.

[10] standard_errors(gamma, rho, data, score_set, phi)

  • Standard errors from the Hessian, multiplied by \(\hat\varphi\) (Equations 5.11 and 5.12).

Returns

  • list(se, correlation). Both are NA with a warning when the estimate lies at a bound or the Hessian cannot be inverted.

[11] fit_model(model, score_set, starts, delta_used = delta, statistic, window, same_rounds)

  • One complete fit of a model. Calls the functions above and forms the aggregate expectation (Equation 5.13) and its error against the SPF mean (Equation 5.14). statistic, window and same_rounds choose the biases as in prepare().

Returns

  • A list with everything from prepare() and estimate(), plus prob, phi, se, correlation and results, a table with one row per scored round. The fits of the run live in fit$A and fit$B (or fit$S).

4.4 Evaluation helpers

[12] rmsfe(error), mafe(error), msfe(error)

  • Root mean squared, mean absolute and mean squared forecast error (Equation 5.14).

[13] with_full_sample(rows)

  • Repeat every row under the regime "Full sample", so that a group_by(regime) also gives the full-sample line.

[14] summarise_fit(model_fit, variation)

  • One row in the layout of the Chapter 6 tables.

[15] both_models(variation, score_set, delta_used = delta)

  • Fit Model A and the second model under one setting from 30 starting values and return their two rows.

[16] show_variations(rows)

  • Print such rows in the thesis layout, each loss as “A / B”. layout_variations() returns the same table without printing it.

Small helpers format numbers (three(), two(), pct(), signed(), wald()), check the parameters (is_number(), is_number_or_na(), is_round()), date the regimes (regime_of()), pick one element from both fits (from_fits()) and name a fit in a warning (fit_label()).

5 Outputs and examples

The chunk below runs main.R with its defaults. Each output is then shown as the script produces it, followed by a variant that calls the functions of Section 4 directly.

source("main.R")

5.1 The sample and the constants

knitr::kable(
  rounds |>
    group_by(regime) |>
    summarise(rounds = n(), first = min(round), last = max(round),
              `mean centre A` = mean(centre_A), `mean centre B` = mean(centre_B)) |>
    arrange(first),
  digits = 2)
cat("Premium of the swap rate:", round(premium, 4), "\n")
Premium of the swap rate: 0.3452 
knitr::kable(data.frame(used      = c(delta, E_star, tau, w),
                        from_data = from_data[c("delta", "E_star", "tau", "w")],
                        row.names = c("delta", "E_star", "tau", "w")), digits = 5)

Output 1: Classification, Table 4.2

classified holds every forecast with its type, shares the three shares per round and model.

Default call:

knitr::kable(table_4_2_shares, digits = 2)

Variant (a band twice as wide):

wide <- prepare("A", delta = 2 * delta)
colSums(wide$counts)                      # hawks, targeters, doves over the 84 scored rounds
    hawk targeter     dove 
     302     2343     1308 
c(hawk_bias = wide$b_up, dove_bias = wide$b_down)
hawk_bias dove_bias 
      1.1       0.8

fit_B_msfe <- fit_model("B", score_settings(tau, w, msfe = TRUE), starting_values(6, 5))
knitr::kable(summarise_fit(fit_B_msfe, "-MSFE"), digits = c(NA, NA, rep(3, 9), 0))

Output 3: Evaluation, Tables 5.4, 5.6 and 5.7

results holds one row per scored round and model. Table 5.6 splits the fit into the centre alone and what switching adds. Table 5.7 starts both models from the announced target alone and adds the location gain.

Default call:

knitr::kable(table_5_4_errors, digits = 3)

knitr::kable(table_5_7_location, digits = c(NA, NA, rep(3, 6), 0))

shares_chosen <- probabilities(gamma = 1, rho = 0.9, fit$A, base_score)

             digits = c(NA, NA, rep(3, 8), 0))
knitr::kable(table_6_3_score |>

                      mafe_elb, gain_elb),

knitr::kable(table_6_4_biases |>
               select(rounds, variation, model, gamma, rho, rmsfe_full, rmsfe_elb, mafe_full,

6 Database catalogue

data/thesis.duckdb holds thirteen tables. The raw tables keep the downloads unchanged and every later table is one cleaning step.

con    <- dbConnect(duckdb(shared_home = FALSE), dbdir = DB_FILE, read_only = TRUE)
tables <- dbReadTable(con, "table_descriptions")
tables$rows <- sapply(tables$table, function(t) dbGetQuery(con, paste("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM", t))$n)
dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
knitr::kable(tables)

The two tables main.R reads:

Table Column Meaning
rounds round, survey_date, target_date Survey round, its survey month and the month its forecast refers to
n_forecasts, spf_mean, spf_sd Point forecasts of the round, their mean and standard deviation
ils 5y5y inflation-linked swap rate of the survey month
hicp Realised HICP inflation in the target month
dfr, regime Deposit facility rate and the regime it dates
lt_mean, lt_target_year Mean SPF five-year-ahead forecast and its target year
estimation_panel round, forecaster, forecast One row per point forecast, 4’173 rows
further columns The round-level series joined to each forecast

The raw sources are listed in the README.

7 Errors you might see

The script checks its parameters before doing any work and says what to change. Five common cases:

  • there is no package called 'dplyr': the packages are not installed yet. Run renv::restore(prompt = FALSE).
  • Database not found: data/thesis.duckdb: run build_database.R.
  • anchor must be "ILS" or "LTSPF" (or a similar message for another parameter): a parameter has a value that is not allowed. The message names the parameter and the allowed values.
  • Standard errors are NA, with a warning that the estimate lies at the bound: \(\gamma\) and \(\rho\) are not identified in that fit. The warning names the model and the settings of the fit, for example Model B, delta 0.4000, tau 0.3994, w 0.0000, which is the row w = 0.0000 of Table 6.3. The estimates and all tables still follow.
  • A DuckDB lock error: another R session has the database open. Close that session.
